program_name: Philosophy International Curriculum (PIC) - the English-taught 'philosophy' curriculum of the Second Cycle Degree in Filosofia (Philosophy). Official names in use: 'Filosofia (International curriculum)' on Apply@UniTo (course id 669); 'Philosophy International Curriculum M.A.' on the programme microsite www.pic.unito.it; the parent degree is 'Corso di Laurea magistrale in Filosofia' (UNITO code 0504M21).
level: master (Italian Laurea magistrale / Second Cycle Degree, 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time; part-time enrolment can be chosen year by year, with tuition varying accordingly). Completion requires submission and defence of a final MA thesis worth 30 ECTS.
teaching_language: CASE 2 - an English pathway inside an Italian-titled degree, but one where the full two years are genuinely delivered in English. The degree itself is the Italian-named 'Corso di Laurea magistrale in Filosofia' (LM-78), which is organised into three curricula: (a) storia della filosofia / history of philosophy (Italian), (b) filosofia teoretica / theoretical philosophy (Italian), and (c) 'philosophy' - the English-taught Philosophy International Curriculum (PIC). The parent degree's own official record therefore lists its language as 'Italiano e Inglese' (Italian and English), while the PIC curriculum is described by UNITO as 'entirely in English' ('interamente in lingua inglese') and by the PIC microsite as 'a fully English-taught MA program'. CONFIRMATION THAT THE FULL 2 YEARS ARE IN ENGLISH: yes. The published PIC curricular flow shows English-taught coursework in BOTH year 1 (Logic and Rationality 12 ECTS, History of Philosophy I, Academic English, plus English-taught options such as Aesthetics, Formal Epistemology and Philosophy of Science, Mind & Language, Philosophy of Language, Philosophy of Religion, Theoretical Philosophy, Western Philosophy of Art) and year 2 (History of Philosophy II, History of Science, plus options such as Aesthetics, Bioethics, Epistemology, Social Ontology, Applied Philosophy, History of Ideas), with the second year dominated by the 30-ECTS MA thesis. The only free-choice component (12 ECTS of electives, two 6-ECTS courses that may be taken in either year) is also constrained to English: 'students choose elective courses (12 ECTS) among all courses (in English) offered at the University of Turin'. Optional Italian-language service courses ('Italian for International Students', beginner or pre-intermediate) exist as a first-year alternative to Academic English, but they are language-support courses, not Italian-medium philosophy teaching. Consequently no Italian-language academic component is required. Apply@UniTo lists the study language of course 669 flatly as 'English'. This is NOT an interuniversity or joint degree: it is a single University of Turin degree run by the Department of Philosophy and Education Science (Dipartimento di Filosofia e Scienze dell'Educazione). PRACTICAL CAVEAT FOR APPLICANTS: because PIC is a curriculum and not a separate degree, the diploma awarded is the Italian Laurea magistrale in Filosofia (class LM-78), the non-EU place quota is shared with the Italian-taught curricula of the same degree, and the Italian-language admission regulation of the parent degree is the governing legal text.
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy. Teaching seat of the parent degree and of PIC: Palazzo Nuovo, via Sant'Ottavio 20, 10124 Turin - the humanities campus of the University of Turin. Governing department: Dipartimento di Filosofia e Scienze dell'Educazione (Department of Philosophy and Education Science); organising structure: Scuola di Scienze Umanistiche (School of Humanities). The academic year in Turin is structured into four teaching blocks of 6-7 weeks plus exam periods (Fall mid-September to end October; Winter mid-November to mid-January with a Christmas break; Spring mid-February to end March; Summer mid-April to end May). For a.y. 2026/27 lectures for some first-year courses start on 14 September 2026. Programme coordinator and chair of the admissions committee for the English curriculum: Prof. Matteo Plebani (matteo.plebani@unito.it); for the Italian-taught curricula the corresponding contact is Prof. Antonella Del Prete (antonella.delprete@unito.it). Student services e-mail: servizistudenti.scienzeumanistiche@unito.it.
degree_class: LM-78 - Scienze filosofiche (Philosophical Sciences). UNITO degree programme code 0504M21; the internal Corso di Studio identifier 005501 also appears in UNITO quality-assurance documents for FILOSOFIA. 120 ECTS over 2 years. Note that UNITO has been migrating degree classes to the reformed 'R' classes (as seen elsewhere in its catalogue); no accessible official page stated an 'LM-78R' designation for this degree, so LM-78 is reported as the class currently published. [uncertain]
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (Italian: 'accesso non programmato' - no numerus clausus, no ranked competition for places) BUT with a compulsory pre-admission eligibility check that must be cleared before enrolment. There is no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT and no written entrance examination. The gate consists of: (1) documented minimum curricular requirements in philosophical subject areas; (2) a preliminary admission application ('Domanda di ammissione preliminare magistrali SUM') evaluated by a committee appointed by the degree programme council; (3) for candidates not automatically admitted, an admission interview (which may be held online via Webex); and (4) specifically for the 'philosophy' (PIC) curriculum, an English language test. Enrolment with formative deficiencies is expressly NOT permitted ('non essendo prevista l'iscrizione con carenze formative') - a candidate short of the required credits must first obtain them, if necessary by enrolling in single courses ('insegnamenti singoli'). TWO SEPARATE APPLICATION CHANNELS APPLY: (A) candidates holding an ITALIAN qualification apply on the www.unito.it / MyUniTo portal via the preliminary admission application; (B) candidates holding a FOREIGN qualification and all international students apply through Apply@UniTo (apply.unito.it), where the Philosophy International Curriculum has its own dedicated course entry, id 669 'Filosofia (International curriculum)'. Because PIC is a curriculum of a larger degree, the non-EU place quota is NOT specific to it: 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. These places are shared among all the curricula of this degree program.' Confirmation that the programme is classified as open access: the deadline shown on the Apply@UniTo course page (8 September 2026) corresponds exactly to UNITO's 'Fourth admission call for OPEN ACCESS postgraduate degree programs only'.
application_deadline_eu: A.Y. 2026/2027. (A) FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION / INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS WHO ARE ITALIANS, EU CITIZENS, EU-EQUIVALENTS OR NON-EU CITIZENS LEGALLY RESIDING IN ITALY - apply via Apply@UniTo. The window shown on the Philosophy International Curriculum course page is the Fourth admission call, reserved to open access postgraduate degree programmes: 25 August - 8 September 2026, with the hard deadline stated as 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time, carrying the notice that the call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. This group could alternatively have used the First admission call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026), which was open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes. A non-refundable EUR 60 application fee must be paid within the deadline of the chosen call. (B) APPLICANTS HOLDING AN ITALIAN QUALIFICATION - do not use Apply@UniTo. They submit the preliminary admission application ('Domanda di ammissione preliminare magistrali SUM') on the www.unito.it portal, open 3 JUNE - 31 DECEMBER 2026 for a.y. 2026-27. Evaluation runs on a rolling calendar with five cut-offs: applications submitted by 14 July receive an answer by 21 July (interview on 18 July, 16:00); by 21 September -> answer by 30 September (interview 29 September, 17:00); by 21 October -> answer by 31 October (interview 30 October, 17:00); by 21 November -> answer by 30 November (interview 27 November, 17:00); by 31 December -> answer by 13 January (interview 11 January, 17:00). Once approved, the actual enrolment ('perfezionamento della procedura di iscrizione') runs 23 July 2026 - 14 January 2027 and must be completed by 14 JANUARY 2027 as set by the Academic Senate; not-yet-graduated candidates may enrol only after obtaining the bachelor's degree and in any case no later than 14 January 2027. Applicants wanting to sit single exams to fill missing credits are advised to register for them by 31 July 2026, and any missing credits must be obtained and reported by 31 December 2026. NOTE: the same official page also contains a residual sentence referring to completing enrolment 'entro la scadenza del 16 gennaio 2026', which appears to be leftover text from the previous cycle and contradicts the 14 January 2027 date given twice elsewhere on the page. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: A.Y. 2026/2027. Non-EU citizens residing abroad (visa applicants) could use ONLY the First admission call on Apply@UniTo: 25 NOVEMBER 2025 - 29 JANUARY 2026, described as 'open to all applicants wishing to apply for postgraduate degree programs'. Every later 2026/2027 call (third, fourth and fifth) is explicitly reserved to Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, and the Philosophy International Curriculum course page carries that restriction verbatim on its currently displayed 8 September 2026 deadline. The 29 January 2026 date is also the deadline for the 'Talents 4 UniTo' scholarship application, which is submitted through Apply@UniTo. Successful non-EU applicants must in addition complete the pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform by the ministerial deadline and complete visa formalities at the competent Italian diplomatic mission; the exact 2026/2027 Universitaly deadline was not verifiable on an accessible official page. As of the research date (1 September 2026) the non-EU-abroad window for 2026/2027 is closed; the equivalent first call for 2027/2028 would be expected around late November 2026 - late January 2027 but is not yet published. Applicants should also note the 50 non-EU-residing-abroad places attached to the Filosofia degree are shared across all three of its curricula, so PIC does not have a ring-fenced non-EU quota of its own. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No standardised admission test (no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT) and no written entrance examination. Two distinct assessment instruments apply, and PIC applicants can face both: (1) AN ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEST, required specifically and only of candidates entering the 'philosophy' (English) curriculum - 'Agli studenti e alle studentesse che intendono iscriversi al curriculum "philosophy" del Corso di Laurea magistrale in Filosofia e richiesta la conoscenza della lingua inglese, da dimostrarsi mediante il superamento di una apposita prova di lingua.' The test dates are not published in advance: candidates admitted to sit it are notified by e-mail, and are separately e-mailed which software/platform will be used. (2) AN ADMISSION INTERVIEW before the admissions committee, which may be held remotely (Webex for the domestic channel; the PIC microsite historically referred to an interview 'possibly via skype' for international candidates). The interview is NOT universal for the domestic channel: candidates who hold the required credits AND an Italian class L-5 (Filosofia) bachelor's degree with a final grade of 75/110 or above are admitted DIRECTLY, their personal preparation being taken as established; candidates coming from other degree classes are summoned to the interview, at which the committee checks the adequacy of their personal philosophical preparation, individual aptitudes and study path. For international applicants through Apply@UniTo, the interview is the stated instrument for language verification: 'Your knowledge of the English language will be verified during the admission interview.' Enrolment can proceed only if the interview and/or the English language test have a positive outcome. Where curricular credits are missing, the committee may instead prescribe specific single exams to be passed before enrolment.
academic_requirements: 1) QUALIFICATION: a three-year first-cycle degree (Italian laurea or diploma universitario di durata triennale) or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as valid under current legislation. Apply@UniTo states it for the international channel as: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education.' Applicants should hold, or be predicted to achieve, an undergraduate degree in philosophy; candidates without a philosophy degree are expressly encouraged to apply provided their exam record contains enough philosophical credits. 2) MINIMUM CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (the core quantitative bar, to be documented with the admission application): (a) at least 60 ECTS/CFU in one or more of the philosophical scientific-disciplinary sectors M-FIL/01 (PHIL-01/A), M-FIL/02 (PHIL-02/A), M-FIL/03 (PHIL-03/A), M-FIL/04 (PHIL-04/A), M-FIL/05 (PHIL-04/B), M-FIL/06 (PHIL-05/A), M-FIL/07 (PHIL-05/B), M-FIL/08 (PHIL-05/C), SPS/02 (GSPS-03/A), IUS/20 (GIUR-17/A); (b) at least 18 of those 60 ECTS must sit in the historical-philosophical sectors M-FIL/06, M-FIL/07, M-FIL/08; (c) a substitution allowance - no more than 18 of the 60 ECTS under (a), and no more than 6 of the 18 ECTS under (b), may be replaced by credits earned in BIO/07 Ecology, INF/01 Computer Science, L-OR/17 Philosophies, religions and history of India and Central Asia, L-LIN/01 Glottology and linguistics, MAT/01 Mathematical logic, M-PED/01 General and social pedagogy, M-PSI/01 General psychology, M-STO/05 History of science and technology, M-STO/06 History of religions, M-STO/07 History of Christianity and the churches, M-STO/08 Archival science, bibliography and librarianship. 3) TOLERANCE MARGIN: a shortfall of up to 10%, i.e. a maximum of 6 ECTS, is admitted, and this margin may be applied to any one or to several of the groups of sectors listed above. 4) THE INTERNATIONAL CHANNEL RESTATES THE BAR IN SIMPLIFIED FORM: 'It is required that you have taken courses in philosophy during the bachelor's degree, for the rough equivalent of 60 ECTS credits' (Apply@UniTo); the PIC microsite phrases it as 'a minimum amount of credits in philosophical subjects (roughly, 60 ECTS credits).' 5) NO ENROLMENT WITH DEFICIENCIES: candidates short of the required credits cannot enrol conditionally; on the committee's indication they may enrol in single courses ('insegnamenti singoli') offered by the University, pass the corresponding exams, and only then enrol in the master's. Missing credits obtained elsewhere must be certified to the chair of the admissions committee (matteo.plebani@unito.it for the English curriculum) by 31 December 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle. 6) GRADE THRESHOLD (domestic route only): holders of the curricular requirements plus an Italian class L-5 bachelor's degree with a final grade of at least 75/110 are admitted directly without interview. There is no published GPA cut-off for foreign qualifications; the international channel is assessed holistically. 7) PERSONAL PREPARATION is assessed by a committee appointed by the degree programme council on the basis of the overall academic record; for the international channel the PIC admissions committee decides on the basis of previous academic achievements evident from CV, diplomas and grades, fit with PIC as shown by the motivation letter and writing sample, and the interview. 8) IT AND FOREIGN-LANGUAGE BASELINE: adequate command of standard IT tools (word processing, presentation software) and adequate knowledge of a foreign language (satisfactory communication, reading and listening skills including academic communication) are taken as already acquired. 9) PLACES: no restricted number of places overall; 50 places are available for non-European applicants residing abroad, shared among all curricula of the Filosofia degree. 10) Foreign qualifications and the adequacy of preparation of holders of foreign academic titles are verified through the University's dedicated procedure for international students; UNITO may subsequently require a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Verification / Statement of Comparability.
language_requirements: ENGLISH - the operative requirement. The expected level is CEFR B2: 'In order to attend the program, students will be expected to have proficiency in English at the B2 level of the Council of Europe framework.' How it is verified differs by channel and this is the single most important practical nuance: (a) DOMESTIC / ITALIAN-QUALIFICATION CHANNEL - English knowledge must be demonstrated by PASSING A DEDICATED LANGUAGE TEST ('mediante il superamento di una apposita prova di lingua'), sat on a calendar communicated by e-mail to candidates admitted to the test, with the platform to be used also communicated by e-mail; this test applies specifically to the 'philosophy' curriculum and not to the Italian-taught curricula. (b) INTERNATIONAL / APPLY@UNITO CHANNEL - the Apply@UniTo course page lists English as the only language requirement and states simply 'Your knowledge of the English language will be verified during the admission interview.' No accessible official page publishes a list of accepted certificates, minimum IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge scores, or explicit exemption rules for native speakers or graduates of English-medium bachelor's degrees, and no page states that a certificate must be uploaded for PIC - the verification appears to be performed in-house by UNITO (test or interview) rather than by certificate. Applicants holding a certificate should nevertheless upload it, since UNITO's general required-documentation page lists 'English language certifications' among the additional documents some postgraduate programmes require. ITALIAN - NOT required for admission and not tested. The Apply@UniTo entry for the English curriculum (course 669) lists English alone under 'Language requirements', in explicit contrast with Italian-taught UNITO programmes: the Italian-taught Filosofia entry (course 603) states that non-EU citizens residing abroad enrolling on an Italian-taught programme must sit an Italian language assessment. That Italian test therefore does not apply to PIC. The Italian-language admission regulation of the parent degree does contain a generic clause (point 6) saying that for holders of foreign academic qualifications the admission requirements and adequacy of personal preparation 'including knowledge of the Italian language' are verified through the University's international-student procedure; this is standard boilerplate written for the degree as a whole, including its Italian-taught curricula, and it sits in tension with the English-only language requirement published for the English curriculum. Italian is instead offered as optional support: PIC students may take 'Italian for International Students' (beginner or pre-intermediate) as a first-year 6-ECTS option in place of Academic English, and the microsite carries a 'Learning Italian' service page. [uncertain]
required_documents: A) FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION / INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS (Apply@UniTo, apply.unito.it course 669): 1) valid passport or identity document; 2) first-cycle (bachelor's) degree certificate obtained after at least 3 years of university education; 3) official transcript of records evidencing roughly 60 ECTS of philosophy courses taken during the bachelor's degree; 4) MOTIVATION LETTER - explicitly listed under 'Other requirements' on the course page ('A motivation letter must be added to your application') and required in English or Italian for all postgraduate programmes; 5) Curriculum Vitae; 6) English language certification where held (listed among the additional documents some postgraduate programmes require); 7) optional but recommended: the degree programme syllabus / course description issued by the foreign institution, with translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish; 8) certified translation of any document not issued in Italian, English, French or Spanish - entry qualification documents are accepted as they are in those four languages; 9) payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call. After submission UNITO may request further documents (Declaration of Value, CIMEA Statement of Verification or Statement of Comparability), and the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment step; incomplete applications are not considered. B) ADDITIONAL PACKAGE RECOMMENDED DIRECTLY BY THE PIC PROGRAMME: to facilitate evaluation, the programme asks candidates to send Prof. Matteo Plebani a single combined PDF containing (i) a short motivation letter introducing yourself and explaining your motivation for enrolling in PIC, (ii) your CV, (iii) your academic credentials, i.e. diploma and transcript of grades, with an explanation of how to interpret the grades where necessary, and (iv) A WRITING SAMPLE - for example the BA thesis or a term paper; if the BA was not in English the writing sample may be submitted in Italian, German, French or Spanish. The writing sample is distinctive to PIC and is one of the three declared bases of the committee's decision, so it should not be treated as optional in practice even though Apply@UniTo does not list it. C) APPLICANTS WITH AN ITALIAN QUALIFICATION (preliminary admission application on the www.unito.it / MyUniTo portal): after logging in - non-UNITO graduates must first register on the UNITO portal - the candidate enters each exam taken specifying its SSD, ECTS and grade, then attaches a self-certification of the exams taken together with the documents proving possession of the minimum curricular requirements set out in point 3 of the admission regulation. Candidates who later obtain missing credits must send a self-certification of the exam(s) to the chair of the admissions committee and open a ticket with the student Service Desk (Category: Polo di Scienze Umanistiche).

For a.y. 2026-27, students resident abroad have the full comprehensive contribution applied directly on the basis of the GDP per capita (PPP) of their country of residence; students whose country appears on the ministerial 'particularly poor countries' list for 2026-2027 are exempt from the comprehensive contribution and pay only the first instalment of EUR 156.00. A separate non-refundable EUR 60 application fee applies to Apply@UniTo submissions. The PIC microsite's own older description of the fee structure (a fixed yearly amount of EUR 580 plus a second income-proportional rate of EUR 0-2,300) predates the current scheme and should not be relied on. SCHOLARSHIPS: https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/scholarships-international-students - for a.y. 2026-2027 UNITO funds 40 two-year 'Talents 4 UniTo' scholarships worth EUR 20,000 gross for international students enrolling in the first year of an OPEN ACCESS postgraduate degree programme held in English, which is exactly the category PIC falls into; the scholarship application is made on Apply@UniTo by the first-call deadline of 29 January 2026 (https://en.unito.it/news/40-two-year-scholarships-international-students-talent-4-unito-ay-2026-2027).

uncertainty_notes:
PATHWAY STATUS (the central point of this record): PIC is a CURRICULUM, not a standalone degree. The legal degree is the Italian-named 'Corso di Laurea magistrale in Filosofia' (LM-78, code 0504M21), which has three curricula - two Italian-taught (history of philosophy; theoretical philosophy) and one English-taught ('philosophy', branded Philosophy International Curriculum / PIC). Practical consequences an applicant must understand: (a) the diploma is a Laurea magistrale in Filosofia, not a separate 'MA in Philosophy International Curriculum'; (b) the binding admission rules are those of the Italian-language regolamento of the parent degree, not the English-language marketing pages; (c) the 50 non-EU places are shared across all three curricula; (d) the English curriculum adds one requirement the Italian curricula do not have - a compulsory English language test. Notwithstanding all this, the ENGLISH DELIVERY IS FULL: both years of coursework are English-taught, the 12 ECTS of free electives must be chosen among English-taught UNITO courses, and the 30-ECTS second-year thesis sits inside an English-taught programme, so a student does not need Italian for academic purposes. This is not an interuniversity or joint degree.

SOURCE ACCESS SITUATION:
- apply.unito.it was reachable directly via curl with a standard desktop browser User-Agent (HTTP 200) on 1 September 2026. Course page 669 (Filosofia - International curriculum), the comparison page 603 (Filosofia, Italian-taught), the 2026/2027 call calendar (news/26) and the required-documentation page (news/13) were all read first-hand and in full. WebFetch alone returns Cloudflare 403 on these, so the UA workaround was essential.
- www.pic.unito.it (the programme microsite, i.e. official_program_url) is unreachable at network level: TLS connections time out / are refused for both WebFetch and curl, with and without a browser User-Agent. Its content was recovered from Wayback Machine raw snapshots: PIC.html (snapshot 2024-06-16, page last updated 2022-06-20), admission_requirements.html (page last updated 2022-06-30), how_to_apply.html (page last updated 2024-04-24), courses.html, contacts.html (last updated 2021-10-11) and tuition_fees_and_financial_aid.html (last updated 2020-04-30).
- filosofialm.campusnet.unito.it is likewise refused on direct fetch, but its Requisiti di ammissione page WAS successfully retrieved via a Wayback raw snapshot and is CURRENT for a.y. 2026/27 - it names the 3 June - 31 December 2026 window, the 14 September 2026 lecture start and the 14 January 2027 enrolment deadline. This is the single most authoritative source in this record for the admission mechanics.
- www.unito.it returned HTTP 403 and en.unito.it was not directly readable; content from those origins (degree class/code, curricula list, tuition, scholarships) comes from indexed search extracts only.

SPECIFIC OPEN POINTS:
1) MICROSITE CONTENT IS STALE. The PIC 'How to apply' page still says 'Classes start on September 2023' and refers to applying for a.y. 2023-24 and to interviews 'possibly via skype'; the fee description on the microsite (EUR 580 fixed plus EUR 0-2,300 income-proportional) predates the current UNITO fee scheme. All PIC-microsite statements about dates and money should be treated as historical; the substantive statements about programme structure, English-only delivery, B2 expectation, the writing-sample requirement and the three decision criteria are corroborated by the current apply.unito.it and filosofialm pages and are treated as reliable.
2) DEGREE CLASS 'R' VARIANT NOT CONFIRMED. LM-78 is the class published for this degree. UNITO has been migrating other degrees to reformed 'R' classes from Cohort 2025, and the admission regulation already uses the new SSD codes in parentheses (PHIL-01/A etc.), which is part of the same reform - so an 'LM-78R' designation for recent cohorts is plausible but was not stated on any page reached. degree_class is marked uncertain.
3) ENROLMENT-DEADLINE CONTRADICTION ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE. The Requisiti di ammissione page states the enrolment window as '23 luglio 2026 - 14 gennaio 2027' and repeats '14 gennaio 2027' as the Senate-set final date, but one earlier paragraph says approved candidates may proceed 'entro la scadenza del 16 gennaio 2026'. The 16 January 2026 date is inconsistent with the rest of the 2026/27 calendar and appears to be un-updated text from the previous cycle. 14 January 2027 is reported as the operative date; application_deadline_eu is marked uncertain for this reason.
4) NON-EU DEADLINE IS INFERRED FROM THE UNIVERSITY-WIDE CALENDAR, not from a PIC-specific statement. The reasoning is sound - the first call (25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026) is the only 2026/27 Apply@UniTo window open to non-EU applicants for postgraduate programmes, and calls three to five are explicitly restricted - but it was not independently confirmed on a PIC-specific page that the programme participated in the first call, and the exact Universitaly pre-enrolment (visa) deadline for 2026/2027 was not verified. application_deadline_non_eu is marked uncertain.
5) ENGLISH VERIFICATION METHOD DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO OFFICIAL CHANNELS and this is a genuine, unresolved inconsistency rather than a research gap: the Italian regolamento mandates a formal English language test ('apposita prova di lingua') for the 'philosophy' curriculum, while the Apply@UniTo page for the same curriculum says English will be verified 'during the admission interview'. It is not stated whether international applicants are additionally required to sit the formal language test, or whether the interview substitutes for it. No accessible page lists accepted certificates, minimum IELTS/TOEFL scores, or exemptions for native speakers or English-medium bachelor's graduates. The B2 level itself is stated only on the (stale) microsite, not on a current page. language_requirements is marked uncertain.
6) ITALIAN-LANGUAGE CLAUSE AMBIGUITY. Point 6 of the parent-degree regulation says that for holders of foreign academic qualifications the admission requirements and adequacy of preparation 'including knowledge of the Italian language' are verified through the University's international-student procedure. Read literally this could imply an Italian requirement for foreign applicants to PIC; read in context it is boilerplate covering the degree as a whole, including its two Italian-taught curricula, and it is contradicted by the Apply@UniTo entry for course 669, which lists English as the only language requirement (in explicit contrast with the Italian-taught Filosofia entry 603, which does impose an Italian test on non-EU applicants residing abroad). The English-only reading is adopted here, but a prospective non-EU applicant would be prudent to confirm with internationalstudents@unito.it.
7) THE 75/110 GRADE RULE IS DOMESTIC-ONLY AND IS AN AUTO-ADMIT, NOT A CUT-OFF. It exempts holders of an Italian class L-5 bachelor's degree from the interview; it does not exclude anyone below it, and it has no published foreign-grade equivalent. There is no published minimum GPA for foreign qualifications.
8) WRITING SAMPLE IS PROGRAMME-REQUESTED, NOT PORTAL-REQUIRED. Apply@UniTo lists only the motivation letter under 'Other requirements'; the writing sample (BA thesis or term paper) is requested by the programme itself, sent directly to the coordinator, and is one of the three declared bases of the committee's decision. It should be treated as effectively mandatory even though the portal does not enforce it. The same applies to the combined-PDF package sent to Prof. Plebani.
9) CURRICULAR-FLOW DATA IS DATED. The course list recovered is labelled for students enrolled in a.y. 2022-2023 with a prospective programme for 2022-23 and a link to a 2023/2024 overview, and one section is marked 'Section being updated'. The structural facts drawn from it (60 ECTS per year, 30-ECTS thesis, 6-ECTS courses except Logic and Rationality at 12 ECTS, 12 ECTS of English-only electives, English-taught coursework across both years) are stable programme architecture, but the specific list of course titles offered in 2026/27 will differ. Note also that the same page lists Italian-titled courses (Bioetica, Teologia politica, Filosofia del diritto, etc.) in its block-by-block timetable - these belong to the wider Filosofia degree offering across all curricula, not to the PIC core, and should not be read as Italian-taught components of PIC.
10) SSD LIST DISCREPANCY. One search-engine summary rendered the philosophical sector list as including SPS/01; the actual regulation text retrieved reads SPS/02 (GSPS-03/A). The page text is authoritative and SPS/02 is reported.
11) NO PIC-SPECIFIC QUOTA OR FEE FIGURE EXISTS. Both the 50 non-EU places and the EUR 156-2,800 fee band are properties of the parent Filosofia degree / the university-wide scheme, not of the curriculum. No PIC-specific intake number, applicant-to-place ratio or selectivity statistic was found on any official page.
12) Per task scope, no polito.it sources were used; all substantive content comes from unito.it origins (apply.unito.it live via UA workaround; pic.unito.it and filosofialm.campusnet.unito.it via Wayback raw snapshots; www.unito.it and en.unito.it via indexed search extracts).
